title: Average salary in Peru 2026 (in USD, by role and city)
summary: The average salary in Peru for a skilled professional runs 600 to 1,200 dollars a month, concentrated in Lima. What it means by role and what hiring there costs.
body_markdown:
The average salary in Peru for a skilled professional is commonly **600 to 1,200 US dollars a month** , concentrated in Lima, with specialised roles in finance, IT, and engineering above that range. Outside the capital the range drops, because Lima holds most of the high-paying demand.


This guide covers what the average salary in Peru actually is in 2026, how it varies by role and by city, what it costs a company to hire there, and why Peru is the quietest of the nearshore markets in a way that works in a hiring company's favour.


## Key takeaways


- Skilled professionals in Lima commonly earn 600 to 1,200 dollars a month.
- Pay outside Lima is lower, and the capital concentrates most of the specialised demand.
- Peru runs at UTC-5 and does not observe daylight saving, so it aligns with US Eastern for most of the year.
- The sol is comparatively stable, so a salary agreed locally holds its value better than in higher inflation markets.
- Cross-border payouts lose 3 to 7 percent to fees and FX before they arrive (McKinsey Global Payments Report, 2026).


## What is the average salary in Peru in 2026?


### The dollar figure


For skilled professionals in Lima the common range is 600 to 1,200 dollars a month. Specialised roles in finance, IT, and engineering sit above it, and roles outside the capital sit below it.


For regional context, the minimum wage across Latin America averaged about 400 dollars a month at the start of 2026 (Statista, 2026), and professional pay in major cities commonly runs 600 to 2,000 dollars a month. The comparison across countries is in[average salary in Latin America](https://www.getontop.com/blog/the-average-salary-in-peru-argentina-mexico-colombia-and-brazil) .


### Lima and everywhere else


Peru's pay map is more concentrated than most of the region. Lima holds the multinational offices, the financial sector, and most of the technical hiring, so the gap between the capital and the rest of the country is wider than the gap between Peru and its neighbours. A national average flattens that and is therefore close to useless for budgeting a specific hire.


## Average salary in Peru by role


Role Common monthly range (USD) Notes


Software engineer Top of the professional range and above Smaller senior pool than Argentina or Colombia


Finance and accounting Upper half of the range Strong presence of multinational back office work in Lima


Engineering (non-software) Upper half of the range Mining and energy pull specialists and pay above market


Customer support Lower half of the range English proficiency varies more than in Colombia


Administrative roles Lower end of the range Widest supply, most price competition


Across Latin America, software engineer base pay runs 30,000 to 63,000 dollars a year, 50 to 70 percent below US levels (Near, 2026). Peru sits toward the lower end of that band, with a smaller senior pool than the larger markets.


## What it costs a company to hire in Peru


### The salary is not the cost


A contractor costs the agreed rate plus a platform fee. An employee costs the salary plus local employer contributions and the overhead of running local payroll. Price the role rather than the country: the[contractor cost by country calculator](https://www.getontop.com/calculator/contractor-cost-by-country) gives current rates for Peru, and the[employee cost calculator](https://www.getontop.com/calculator/employee-cost) adds the contributions that a contractor rate does not include.


### Why Peru is worth a look


Peru is overlooked next to Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Argentina, and that is the argument for it. The time zone matches US Eastern for most of the year, the talent exists, and fewer foreign employers are bidding for it. Companies willing to source beyond the obvious hubs find less competition at the offer stage and lower turnover afterwards. The regional models are laid out in[nearshore hiring in Latin America](https://www.getontop.com/solutions/nearshore-hiring-latin-america) .


## Paying a Peruvian salary cleanly


### Local currency or dollars


The sol has been comparatively stable, so unlike higher inflation markets the choice of currency is a preference rather than a survival question. Many professionals working with foreign clients still prefer to hold dollars, because their income is priced internationally even when their costs are local. Offering both is the answer that survives contact with a real team, and workers paid into an[Ontop Global Account](https://www.getontop.com/ontop-global-account) can hold dollars and convert on their own schedule.


### What you send is not what lands


Cross-border payouts lose 3 to 7 percent to fees and FX before arriving (McKinsey Global Payments Report, 2026). On a 1,000 dollar salary that is up to 70 dollars a month that the worker never sees and the company still paid. The mechanics are in[multi-currency payroll](https://www.getontop.com/blog/managing-multiple-currencies-international-payroll-strategies) , and the company side without entities is in[global contractor payroll](https://www.getontop.com/solutions/global-contractor-payroll) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the average salary in Peru in US dollars?


For skilled professionals in Lima, commonly 600 to 1,200 dollars a month, with specialised roles in finance, IT, and engineering above that. Pay outside Lima is lower.


### What is the average monthly salary in Peru?


Professional pay commonly falls between 600 and 1,200 dollars a month. The Latin American minimum wage averaged about 400 dollars a month at the start of 2026 (Statista, 2026).


### What is the average income in Peru compared with its neighbours?


Peru sits in the middle to lower part of the regional professional range, close to Colombia and below Brazil and Mexico in dollar terms.


### Is Lima more expensive than the rest of Peru?


Yes, for both cost of living and salaries. Lima concentrates the specialised roles and the multinational employers, which pulls pay above the national picture.


### Can a foreign company hire in Peru without an entity?


Yes. Contractors can be engaged and paid directly, and employees can be hired through an employer of record. An entity only pays off at sustained local headcount.


### How much does it cost to hire a developer in Peru?


Substantially less than a comparable US hire, with the exact figure set by seniority and hiring model. The senior pool is smaller than in the larger markets, so scarce specialists price closer to regional leaders than the country average suggests.


## What to do next


Budget the landed amount rather than the headline: the rate, plus contributions if you are employing, minus what conversion takes on the way in. That number is what the person actually receives, and it is what decides whether your offer is competitive in Lima.
